xpath.p:
On the booking page the customer picks this therapy, reads the description, then chooses one of its session packages (the products filed under this category). These questions are asked once, whichever package they choose.
Name your sections in Question Headings above, then pick one in a question's Heading. Questions sharing a heading are shown as one block wherever they are asked, and the sections follow the order of the headings list - not the questions list. Leave the heading empty for a question that belongs to no section. A heading you have just added only appears in the dropdown once this therapy is saved.
Heading Colour, Bold, Italic and Underline are set once above and apply to every section title of this therapy, wherever the questions are asked - in the POS, on the tablet and on the booking page. Leave the colour empty to keep the colour each screen uses by default.
Use the delete icon at the end of a row to remove a question or a heading. Deleting a heading only unfiles its questions, it does not delete them; a question that customers have already answered is archived rather than deleted, so their answers stay on their record.
The Disclaimer is shown on a page of its own, straight after the questions, in the POS, on the tablet and on the booking page - the customer reads it there, ticks that they agree and signs. Format it with the editor toolbar - bold a clause heading, colour a warning, add a list - and it is shown that way on every screen. The customer's name, number and email are filled in underneath it automatically from what was already entered, so a "Client Information" block does not need typing into the text.
Turn Show Disclaimer Page off to hide that page without losing a word of it - the wording stays here ready to switch back on. Note that with it off the customer is not asked to accept terms and does not sign for this therapy, so no signed consent is recorded. The page is also skipped if you leave the wording empty.
Turn Allow Signature Upload on to let staff attach a picture of the signature on that page instead of the customer drawing it. Off by default - a consent signature is normally signed on the spot.
